subject: Proposed leadership nominations + geo-squad alignment — comms draft
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Thu, 18 Mar 2027 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed leadership nominations + geo-squad alignment — comms draft

Team,

Attached is a first-pass comms draft and the updated org chart for the proposed geo-squad alignment we discussed in leadership last week. High-level context: this is a targeted set of leadership nominations and small role moves intended to better align product leadership by region (US / EU / APAC) and to create two cross-functional "geo squads" that own latency/cost OKRs per region. The goal is to make decision ownership closer to the users and reduce cross-region coordination overhead for Q3.

Attachments: org-chart-v2.pdf, lead-nom-list.xlsx

Asks:
- Read the draft and the nominees list; I need final feedback by EOD next Friday (2027-03-26) so we can finalize slides for the QBR.
- Please call out any wording you think will cause unnecessary concern; we want the announcement to be clear on rationale (customer impact, latency/cost OKRs) and signal that individual contributors' roles are stable except where noted.
- Approve or flag any nomination changes (I highlighted the ones we haven't confirmed with candidates).

Draft plan for timing: internal leadership review -> small-group town hall (managers) -> all-engineers announcement + Q&A in the QBR. We will include a short FAQ and org-chart on the announcement page.

I included an outline of QBR talking points in the doc link above; happy to seed slides if agreed.

Thanks —
Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of People Operations
Redwood Inference


From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: Fri, 19 Mar 2027 10:15:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed leadership nominations + geo-squad alignment — comms draft

Thanks for the draft, Olga — nice clean framing. A few quick thoughts after skimming:

1) Tone: emphasize continuity and customer impact up front. The current opening dives into structure; flip that so the first paragraph is "why this helps customers / reduces latency and cost".

2) Timing: can we make the effective date explicit in the comms? Suggest "effective May 1, 2027" unless a candidate needs a later start. That gives managers time to adjust team plans and OKRs.

3) OKR tie-in: add a one-paragraph "impact on OKRs" that maps the geo squads to the three Q3 objectives (Latency SLOs, Cost/unit, Reliability). I mocked a short version in qbr-talking-points-draft.docx (attached).

4) Nominations: agree we should avoid naming folks who haven't accepted. For the ones highlighted as tentative, call them out as "pending acceptance" and propose two alternatives per slot.

I'll inline-edit the opening paragraph and share a few sample bullets if helpful.

Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Product Operations
Redwood Inference

Cc: 
Date: Sat, 20 Mar 2027 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Proposed leadership nominations + geo-squad alignment — comms draft

Appreciate the work on this, Olga. A few practical notes from product leadership POV:

- For any product leader moves that change owner for an active roadmap, please include an explicit "handoff checklist" item in the comms (knowledge transfer, outstanding PRs, active OKR owners). We should avoid surprises during sprint planning.
- On nominations: one suggested swap — consider Markus Klein for the EU product lead role if Markus confirms availability. If Markus isn't available, we should call out the external hiring fallback.
- Recommend adding a short "contingencies" section: if acceptance / hiring extends past May 1, we'll gate any disruptive changes until after the QBR. That protects ongoing deliverables.

I made a couple of line edits in the doc linked in your message.

-Vivek
Vivek Kulkarni
Chief Product Officer
